edges.effect_quant: The best parity-aware syntheses still support a protective association. A 2014 meta-analysis of 40 epidemiologic studies including 17,139 women with ovarian cancer found that, among parous women only, breastfeeding was associated with lower ovarian cancer risk (pooled RR 0.76, 95% CI 0.69 to 0.83), and risk fell further with longer total duration.
edges.population: parous women evaluated for epithelial ovarian cancer risk with breastfeeding duration analyzed separately from parity
edges.mechanism: Breastfeeding suppresses ovulation and lowers exposure to gonadotropins and cyclic ovarian epithelial turnover, which may reduce opportunities for malignant transformation. The persistence of protective estimates after parity adjustment suggests breastfeeding contributes risk reduction beyond pregnancy count alone.
edges.summary: The evidence supports a protective association independent of simple parity count. Meta-analytic and large case-control data show lower ovarian cancer risk in women who breastfed, with stronger protection at longer durations and after statistical adjustment for parity.
edges.caveats: Most evidence is observational and much of it comes from case-control studies, so recall bias and residual confounding remain possible. Some individual studies found attenuation after parity adjustment, meaning the incremental effect of breastfeeding beyond childbearing is real but probably modest rather than huge.

evidence.citation: LiDP et al 2014 Asian Pac J Cancer Prev
evidence.notes: Breastfeeding and ovarian cancer risk: a systematic review and meta-analysis of 40 epidemiological studies.

effect_quant.comparator: ovarian cancer in parous women who breastfed versus parous women who never breastfed in the parity-restricted pooled analysis
